searchText: so i know we're all about BAL as our endgame solution for tx parallelization, and i'm all for that. but i think we can do something really quick, and really high leverage to get more clients able to run parallel transactions the way besu does. i've started a draft EIP here: https://github.com/jflo/EIPs/pull/2/files but the idea is, if a client knows that a subset of transactions in its block are independent, it can include that list in the block as a hint for other clients to execute in parallel it's a work in progress, looking for feedback, TIA. Could include full list (1 integer per tx) of last tx index that tx is dependent on. Probably needs to be 1-based and then 0 as not dependent. So 1 byte per independent tx Would that be enough to build full parallelization dag? 🤔 It would, but also becomes harder to compute for builders. Just identifying the independent ones gets a useful portion of the block in parallel for little work I.e can do simpler approaches like marking slots as dirty mark dirty with tx number (last written); then highest dirty number read is last dependency Is that easy in nethermind? Maybe(ish); add extra numeric to the block cache with value [address+slot] = { value, txIndex } txIndex as -1 if only read though that doesn't work for rlp Can change that, request bodies are opaque I mean 1 based with 0 being independent would be easier <dankrad> all the computational work here is part of executing the transactions, there is no meaningful extra computation to be done (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Justin Florentine> It would, but also becomes harder to compute for builders. Just identifying the independent ones gets a useful portion of the block in parallel for little work) ah, actaully would fall down if a later tx writes to something an earlier tx reads, but is executed before it <dankrad> I would suggest a different solution though (that Toni is working on): transaction-level state diffs (include all values written by a transaction). This allows parallel execution even for the "dirty" transactions as you will just get the pre-state from the transaction that came before it Yes, I’m aware of the BAL work, this is designed to be an interim parallelization boost, it doesn’t do many of the things BAL does, but could be shipped quick. High leverage Clients have to just not fail on the new request type, and everything else is optional Have you guys seen this idea for BALs to include a bloom filter? Then this filter in particular (once negated) proves what is NOT accessed and this can prove that a tx is independent (based on the acceses of that tx compared with the access filter). See https://ethresear.ch/t/block-level-access-lists-bals/22331/2?u=jochem-brouwer Idea by <@857052906495017000> (could replace logsBloom in block header 👀 ) Make -1 encoded as empty list 😛 😄 Have left a reply on PR, per this rq type it will end up in `block.header.requestsHash` so this thing cannot be optional 😅 Debate on 7907 Debate on 7907 is there a way to do paralellism that gives improved guarantees about the worst case block execution time? because without such guarantees it doesn't really enable a higher gas limit. if you have BAL's with state images and max tx sizes you get certain guarantees, but even then it might be hard Can we also have someone from Besu and Reth in this thread? 🙂 Don't want to ping the entire besu/reth group (cant ping reth but can ping besu? 🤔 ) <@827653956955406406> <@429719902363058177> could you maybe delegate someone here?

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: so i know we're all about BAL as our endgame solution for tx parallelization, and i'm all for that. but i think we can do something really quick, and really high leverage to get more clients able to run parallel transactions the way besu does.

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: i've started a draft EIP here: https://github.com/jflo/EIPs/pull/2/files

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: but the idea is, if a client knows that a subset of transactions in its block are independent, it can include that list in the block as a hint for other clients to execute in parallel

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: it's a work in progress, looking for feedback, TIA.

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content:
Could include full list (1 integer per tx) of last tx index that tx is dependent on. Probably needs to be 1-based and then 0 as not dependent. So 1 byte per independent tx

Would that be enough to build full parallelization dag? 🤔

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: It would, but also becomes harder to compute for builders. Just identifying the independent ones gets a useful portion of the block in parallel for little work

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: I.e can do simpler approaches like marking slots as dirty

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: mark dirty with tx number (last written); then highest dirty number read is last dependency

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: Is that easy in nethermind?

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: Maybe(ish); add extra numeric to the block cache with value

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: [address+slot] = { value, txIndex }

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: txIndex as -1 if only read

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: though that doesn't work for rlp

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: Can change that, request bodies are opaque

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: I mean 1 based with 0 being independent would be easier

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dankrad> all the computational work here is part of executing the transactions, there is no meaningful extra computation to be done (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Justin Florentine> It would, but also becomes harder to compute for builders. Just identifying the independent ones gets a useful portion of the block in parallel for little work)

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: ah, actaully would fall down if a later tx writes to something an earlier tx reads, but is executed before it

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dankrad> I would suggest a different solution though (that Toni is working on): transaction-level state diffs (include all values written by a transaction). This allows parallel execution even for the "dirty" transactions as you will just get the pre-state from the transaction that came before it

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: Yes, I’m aware of the BAL work, this is designed to be an interim parallelization boost, it doesn’t do many of the things BAL does, but could be shipped quick. High leverage

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: Clients have to just not fail on the new request type, and everything else is optional

excerpts.content: Have you guys seen this idea for BALs to include a bloom filter? See https://ethresear.ch/t/block-level-access-lists-bals/22331/2?u=jochem-brouwer Idea by <@857052906495017000>
